# SEGAN Reproduction — Step-by-Step User Guide

**Research article:** F. F. Aydin, “Auditable state-based screening of capacity-withholding effects in nodal electricity markets,” *Sustainable Energy, Grids and Networks*, vol. 48, article 102558, 2026. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.segan.2026.102558

**Purpose:** Reproduce Figures 2–7 and Tables 4–9 from the published research. Figure 1 was prepared manually for the article and is not generated by this software. The repository performs **reported-offer DC-OPF and post-hoc true-cost accounting**, not an AMES agent-based market simulation. AMES contributes benchmark-style input data and economic concepts.

**Bundled release design:** The repository is prepared to include all **four validated raw inputs** in `data/raw/` and all **twelve verified Quick checkpoints** in `outputs/cache/`. Links to the original AMES, PGLib, MATPOWER, Kaggle and EPİAŞ sources are given for provenance and optional independent acquisition; users do **not** need to download data separately when they receive the complete release. Third-party licensing and provenance are reviewed separately from the author's approval to share their code and own derived outputs. The release is not public until those final checks and an explicit software license are settled.

## 1. Select the reproduction route

| Route | What you need | What the program computes | What it produces |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Quick** | Twelve validated `.mat` checkpoints in `outputs/cache/`, compatible MATLAB and plotting/statistics functions | Reconstructs graphics and publication tables from the stored results; **no new OPF or K-means** | Figures 2–7 and Tables 4–9 in `quick_reproduction/outputs/` |
| **Full** | Four canonical local raw inputs, MATLAB, MATPOWER, an appropriately licensed DC-OPF solver, Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox | Repeats DC-OPF, generator screening, economic calculations, K-means, K-sensitivity, ablations and exports | Newly computed `.mat` checkpoints plus Figures 2–7 and Tables 4–9 in `outputs/` |

Quick and Full use the *same* publication-export code. Quick is a results-based regeneration, not an independent recomputation of the paper's hourly optimizations.

## 2. Required software and published environment

For best comparability, use the versions reported in the article:

| Software | Reference configuration | Where to get it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MATLAB | R2025b Update 3 | https://www.mathworks.com/products/matlab.html |
| Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox | Required for K-means and PCA | https://www.mathworks.com/products/statistics.html |
| MATPOWER | 8.1 | https://matpower.org/download/ |
| Gurobi Optimizer | 13.0.1 | https://www.gurobi.com/product/download-center |
| Gurobi academic license | User must qualify and activate their own | https://support.gurobi.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040541251-How-do-I-obtain-a-free-academic-license |

MATPOWER and Gurobi are installed **separately**. Neither installer nor any Gurobi license file is part of this repository. Version availability, platform support and licensing requirements may change. Different versions or solver choices can produce numeric differences.

### 2A. Install and open MATLAB

1. Install and activate a compatible 64-bit MATLAB release through your own MathWorks account or institution.
2. Ensure **Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox** is installed (MATLAB **Home > Add-Ons > Manage Add-Ons**, where available).
3. Open MATLAB and use the **Command Window** for the commands below.
4. Confirm the environment:

```matlab
version
ver
which('kmeans')
which('pca')
```

`kmeans` and `pca` should resolve to installed toolbox implementations. If they do not, correct the toolbox installation before running Full Mode.

### 2B. Install MATPOWER 8.1 and connect it to MATLAB

1. Download MATPOWER **8.1** from https://matpower.org/download/ and extract it to a directory of your choice, **outside the SEGAN project**.
2. In the MATLAB Current Folder browser, navigate to the extracted MATPOWER directory containing `install_matpower.m`.
3. Enter:

```matlab
install_matpower
```

4. Follow the official interactive prompts to add the required folders to the MATLAB path. If there is only one installed MATPOWER version, choose the option that also **saves** the path when appropriate.
5. Verify:

```matlab
which('rundcopf')
which('mpoption')
test_matpower
```

The built-in MATPOWER test suite may run many tests. See the official installation guide: https://matpower.org/about/get-started/ . Do not copy MATPOWER itself into `src/+segan/`.

### 2C. Install Gurobi and connect it to MATLAB

1. Download and install Gurobi from https://www.gurobi.com/product/download-center . Gurobi **13.0.1** was used in the reference environment; if you use a different release, record it.
2. Obtain and activate a license appropriate for your use. Eligible academic users can request an academic license. Gurobi describes the Named-User and WLS licensing options and their network requirements at https://support.gurobi.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040541251-How-do-I-obtain-a-free-academic-license . **Never commit `gurobi.lic`, access keys, or credentials.**
3. Open MATLAB and navigate to the `matlab` subdirectory **inside your installed Gurobi directory**. It should contain `gurobi_setup.m`. For example, use MATLAB's Current Folder browser rather than assuming a fixed installation path.
4. Run:

```matlab
gurobi_setup
which('gurobi')
```

5. Follow the setup output if it asks you to save the MATLAB path. The Gurobi MATLAB interface is supplied by the **full Gurobi installation**; installing `gurobipy` with `pip` does not by itself install the MATLAB interface.
6. If a license error occurs, follow the instructions in the Gurobi User Portal and the official license documentation; do not put license files in this repository.

Official instructions: https://docs.gurobi.com/projects/optimizer/en/current/reference/matlab/setup.html and https://support.gurobi.com/hc/en-us/articles/4533938303505-How-do-I-install-Gurobi-for-Matlab .

**Reference solver setting:** the study uses `opf.dc.solver = 'DEFAULT'`. MATPOWER chooses an available algorithm; `DEFAULT` **does not guarantee GUROBI on another computer**. After preparing Stage 1 inputs, you can check the actual solver selection in the local environment using the optional probe described in Section 5. The reported local probe resolved to GUROBI but did not retrospectively log every solver choice of the earlier Full run.

## 3. Locate the four bundled raw inputs

A complete SEGAN release contains the **exact validated files** below under `data/raw/` (do not rename or substitute them):

```text
data/raw/
  AMES_5Bus.xlsx
  case57.m
  pglib_opf_case57_ieee__sad.m
  power Generation and consumption.csv
```

| Input | Where to start | Important compatibility note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AMES_5Bus.xlsx` | Official AMES test-bed materials: https://faculty.sites.iastate.edu/tesfatsi/archive/tesfatsi/AMESMarketHome.htm | The bundled **author-prepared workbook** is the exact input used in the validated calculations. The AMES web page is credited as an upstream scientific source, not as a guaranteed download of this identical workbook. |
| `case57.m` | MATPOWER 8.1 installation, https://matpower.org/download/ | The bundled, validated file is available under `data/raw/`. The MATPOWER installation supplies an independent reference; MATPOWER's software BSD license does **not** automatically cover its case data. |
| `pglib_opf_case57_ieee__sad.m` | PGLib-OPF: https://github.com/power-grid-lib/pglib-opf | Preserve the exact SAD benchmark/version and file attribution. PGLib lists data under CC BY 4.0, subject to case-specific attribution. |
| `power Generation and consumption.csv` | Kaggle study source: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/dharanikra/electrical-power-demand-in-turkey ; underlying public data: https://seffaflik.epias.com.tr/ | The bundled, validated CSV has the exact schema used for the paper. The public Kaggle/EPİAŞ links are given for independent comparison; substituting a newly downloaded export may require conversion and new validation. |

**No user input preprocessing is necessary for the bundled canonical files.** Keep the supplied bytes unchanged. If a reader independently replaces any input, they must preserve or reconstruct the validated format, check the data-source license, and revalidate all results. See `RELEASE_DATA_SHA256.tsv` for integrity checks. The author approves sharing this project and these packaged research inputs, while third-party source conditions (especially the MATPOWER `case57` data and external workbook/CSV provenance) require separate attribution/rights review before public release.

## 4. Open the SEGAN project inside MATLAB

1. Download and extract the **SEGAN repository source**. Keep its folder hierarchy intact.
2. Open MATLAB. In the **Current Folder** panel, navigate to the repository root, the folder that contains `reproduce_all.m` and `config/`.
3. Run:

```matlab
addpath(fullfile(pwd, 'config'));
addpath(fullfile(pwd, 'src'));
rehash;
cfg = reproduction_config();
```

4. Confirm file/function accessibility:

```matlab
which('reproduce_all')
which('rundcopf')
which('gurobi')
which('kmeans')
```

The configured SEGAN code uses **relative paths**; do not edit MATLAB source files to paste your personal Windows path. The repository root is established from where MATLAB runs.

## 5. Run safe environment checks and a small demo

**Full planning check (read-only):**

```matlab
plan = reproduce_all('plan');
disp(plan.SafeToStartFreshRun);
disp(plan.Stages);
```

The output should indicate that all 23 stages, all four raw files and required dependencies are available. `SafeToStartFreshRun = 0` is **intentional** if `outputs/` already contains generated files.

**Small demonstration:** The demo requires the first-stage prepared input MAT checkpoint. In an empty working copy, the input preparation stage writes its input cache; then the demo solves four small cases in memory:

```matlab
cfg = reproduction_config();
inputs = segan.prepare_inputs(cfg);
demo = run_demo();
disp(demo.Validation);
```

Do not run this preparation step in a directory where you are trying to preserve an already-complete validated output tree.

**Check actual DC-OPF solver selection (optional):** after Stage 1 exists:

```matlab
evidence = segan.probe_dc_solver(cfg);
disp(evidence.Cases);
disp(evidence.Validation);
```

This small probe compares the configured solver request with explicit GUROBI in peak-hour examples and leaves research files unchanged. It is evidence about **this** run and environment, not historical proof of earlier Full computations.

## 6. Quick Mode: regenerate figures and tables from checkpoints

1. Verify the **twelve bundled MAT checkpoints** are already in `outputs/cache/` with their original names. Do not substitute arbitrary MAT files.
2. Ensure `quick_reproduction/outputs/` contains **no existing generated files**.
3. Start MATLAB from the repository root and run:

```matlab
addpath(fullfile(pwd, 'config'));
addpath(fullfile(pwd, 'src'));
quickPlan = reproduce_all('quick_plan');
assert(quickPlan.SafeToStartQuickRun, 'Quick input or destination check failed.');
quickReport = reproduce_all('quick');
disp(quickReport.Validation);
assert(quickReport.Validation.AllPassed);
```

On the validated workstation this produced **27 nonempty files**: six figure PNGs, six figure PDFs, six table CSVs, six table TeX files and three plotting-data CSVs. No OPF or K-means was rerun. The command intentionally refuses to overwrite an occupied Quick destination.

## 7. Full Mode: rebuild everything from the bundled raw data

**Important:** The downloadable repository contains 12 Quick MAT files under `outputs/cache/`, so `reproduce_all('full')` must **not** be called in the original downloaded root. Full Mode checks that the `outputs/` tree is empty to prevent overwriting validated results.

**Create a clean workspace from inside MATLAB (without moving source files by hand):**

```matlab
% Current Folder: downloaded SEGAN repository root
addpath(fullfile(pwd,'config'),'-begin');
addpath(fullfile(pwd,'src'),'-begin');
planWorkspace = prepare_full_workspace('plan');
disp(planWorkspace);
assert(planWorkspace.SafeToCreate, 'Full workspace already exists or inputs are incomplete.');
workspace = prepare_full_workspace();  % Copies code + four raw inputs only.
cd(workspace.WorkspacePath);
addpath(fullfile(pwd,'config'),'-begin');
addpath(fullfile(pwd,'src'),'-begin');
clear functions;
rehash;
plan = reproduce_all('plan');
disp(plan.SafeToStartFreshRun);
assert(plan.SafeToStartFreshRun, 'Full workspace preflight failed.');
```

Then, **from that newly created workspace**:

```matlab
report = reproduce_all('full');
disp(report.Validation);
```

The helper creates `full_workspace/` under the downloaded project, copies only `config/`, `src/`, `tests/`, essential entrypoint code and the **four bundled raw files**, and creates an empty `outputs/` tree. It does **not** copy the 12 Quick MAT files, any previously generated scenarios, figures or tables. It never overwrites an existing `full_workspace/`; if the creation fails halfway through, preserve the incomplete directory and diagnose the error rather than deleting blindly.

Full Mode runs 23 stages, repeating the 5-bus and 57-bus OPF, generator screening, state analysis, K-sensitivity, ablation, and publications. Results appear under **that workspace's** `outputs/` directory. A full run can require substantial computing resources; records may differ at the binary-file level while validated numerical results agree within published rounding tolerances.

On completion:

```matlab
check = validate_results();
disp(check.Validation);
```

Keep the full run log and report your MATLAB/MATPOWER/Gurobi versions. Do not rerun Full Mode on an occupied or partially complete output directory; the safety guard intentionally blocks it.

## 8. Verify and find results

```matlab
results = validate_results();
disp(results.Validation);
testResults = runtests(fullfile(pwd, 'tests', 'test_reproduction.m'));
disp(testResults);
```

Expected paths after Full:

```text
outputs/cache/                       Computed MAT checkpoints and scenario records
outputs/figures/Figure_2.png ... Figure_7.pdf
outputs/tables/Table_4.csv ... Table_9.tex
```

Quick outputs have the same `figures/` and `tables/` subfolders under `quick_reproduction/outputs/`. The image export may show a MATLAB vectorization warning while successfully creating a PDF; inspect the produced file before classifying a warning as failure.

## 9. Understanding the results

- The paper distinguishes **reported market offers** used in DC-OPF from **baseline true costs** used for ex-post net-earnings accounting.
- Some economic outputs represent **90-day totals**, and the code preserves this in names such as `...90Days`; do not relabel the totals as daily averages. The paper's selected table units should be interpreted carefully.
- Unsupervised K-means cluster IDs are arbitrary; use economic cluster interpretation and label-invariant comparison metrics rather than expecting numeric labels to be universally fixed.
- The research provides a transparent screening method; it **does not infer an individual generator's intent or establish legal market manipulation**.

## 10. Common installation and reproduction problems

| Symptom | Likely cause / remedy |
| --- | --- |
| `Undefined function 'rundcopf'` or `mpoption` | Install MATPOWER 8.1; run `install_matpower`; verify `which('rundcopf')`. |
| `Undefined function 'gurobi'` | Run `gurobi_setup` from the Gurobi MATLAB installation directory, then `which('gurobi')`. |
| `Gurobi license` / `No valid license` | Activate your own eligible license using official Gurobi instructions; never copy another user's license. |
| `Undefined function 'kmeans'` or `pca` | Install Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox and confirm it is on the path. |
| Input file missing, invalid sheets/headers | Check the **four exact filenames** and canonical workbook/CSV structure. Renaming an incompatible export is not sufficient. |
| `SafeToStartFreshRun = 0` | Full Mode sees a populated output tree or a missing requirement. Use a new clean working copy and read the plan report. |
| `SafeToStartQuickRun = 0` | One of twelve checkpoints is missing or Quick destination is occupied; check `quickPlan.RequiredMAT`. |
| `DEFAULT` resolves to another solver | MATPOWER chooses among installed solvers; record the algorithm and version, and do not claim exact reference-solver parity without evidence. |
| Result differs slightly from article | Check exact input versions, MATLAB/MATPOWER/Gurobi releases, random seed, solver and 90-day-vs-per-day accounting; consult the numerical validation report. |
| Figure PDF vectorization warning | Inspect the generated PDF/PNG; a warning alone does not mean the export failed. |
| Repository location includes Turkish letters or spaces | Use MATLAB `fullfile(pwd,...)` and the Current Folder browser; do not handcraft a hard-coded user path. |

## 11. Obtaining help and citing the article

For changes or issues, provide: MATLAB version, MATPOWER version, Gurobi version (without license secrets), the exact failing stage/line, and the **relevant log excerpt**. Do not upload private licensing files.
